data.summary: This 16‑week plan focuses first on the weak Unit 1 topics, then builds through the remaining units while keeping each week within the 5‑hour limit. Live class #10800 is scheduled in week 2 to reinforce early limits material. The final two weeks are devoted to mixed review and timed practice to solidify all concepts before the exam.
data.final_week_advice: Use the last two weeks for full‑length practice exams and targeted review of any remaining weak spots; keep the pace steady and avoid new topics.

tasks: Read textbook sections on 1.1–1.3 and write a summary of each concept.
Do 15 practice limit problems from 1.2 and 1.3, marking each answer with the scoring guide.
Create a flashcard deck for key limit properties from 1.5.
Attend live class #10800 covering 1.1–1.3.
Review class notes and solve 10 additional limit problems.
Begin 2.1 by sketching graphs of average rates for two sample functions.

weeks.focus: Deepen limit skills and derivative definition
tasks: Solve 20 limit problems using tables (1.4).
Work through 1.5 algebraic limit properties with 15 practice questions.
Read 2.2 derivation of derivative notation and write a step‑by‑step explanation.

weeks.focus: Estimate derivatives and connect to continuity
tasks: Estimate derivatives for 10 functions using graph and table data (2.3).
Solve 10 problems linking differentiability and continuity (2.4).
Create a concept map linking limits, continuity, and derivatives.

weeks.focus: Power rule and chain rule basics
tasks: Practice 20 power rule problems (2.5).
Solve 10 chain rule examples (3.1).
Write a short reflection on when to use each rule.
Do 15 implicit differentiation problems (3.2).
Solve 10 inverse function derivative problems (3.3).
Summarize key differences between the two techniques.

weeks.focus: Inverse trig and related rates intro
tasks: Practice 10 inverse trig derivatives (3.4).
Solve 5 related rates problems (4.4).
Create a checklist for setting up related rates equations.
Read MVT proof and apply to 5 problems (5.1).
Solve 10 problems on global vs local extrema (5.2).
Draw graphs illustrating critical points.
Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 8 functions (5.3).
Apply first derivative test to 6 functions (5.4).
Create a decision tree for choosing the right test.
Approximate area under 5 curves using Riemann sums (6.2).
Solve 5 problems on accumulation functions (6.1).
Review FTC statement and solve 5 FTC application problems (6.4).
Model 3 real‑world scenarios with differential equations (7.1).
Verify solutions for 4 equations (7.2).
Write a short report on modeling assumptions.
Sketch slope fields for 3 differential equations (7.3).
Use slope fields to predict behavior in 4 scenarios (7.4).
Create a visual guide for interpreting slope fields.
Compute average values for 5 functions (8.1).
Relate position, velocity, and acceleration via integrals for 3 examples (8.2).
Summarize key formulas in a cheat sheet.

weeks.focus: Applied integrals and area between curves
tasks: Solve 5 applied integral problems (8.3).
Find area between curves for 4 pairs of functions (8.4).
Create a step‑by‑step worksheet for area calculations.
Take a full-length timed practice exam covering all units.
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide.
Identify 5 weak areas and review the corresponding topics.
Review flashcards for all key concepts.
Do 10 timed free‑response questions on the most challenging topics.
Outline a pre‑exam routine and mental checklist.
